children.text: New in Pro 1.11.0: connect your AI assistant and your own scripts
Bot-Free Meeting Notes for Engineering and Product Teams

Meetily is a bot-free AI meeting assistant for engineering and product teams who want standups, sprint planning and incident reviews transcribed on their own machines. It records your computer's audio on Windows or macOS, so no bot joins the Zoom, Teams or Google Meet call, and Whisper or Parakeet transcribes it 100% locally. With Meetily Pro, your own script or AI assistant can read the summary and file the action items as Jira, Linear or GitHub issues.
WORKS WITH ZOOM, TEAMS & GOOGLE MEET
Built for the Meetings Engineering Teams Actually Have
Standups, sprint planning, incident reviews and architecture discussions, captured without a bot and transcribed on the machine that recorded them.
Meetily records your computer's system audio, so it works with Zoom, Microsoft Teams, Google Meet, Slack Huddles, Discord and Webex. Nobody has to admit a recorder into the standup.

Whisper or Parakeet runs 100% locally on Windows and macOS (Apple Silicon), so roadmap talk and unreleased architecture never reach a transcription vendor. For summaries you pick a local model or your own API key.
Who Said What, in the Shape You Need
Pro's speaker diarization labels each speaker, and custom summary templates shape the notes for a sprint planning, retro or incident review. Export to Markdown, PDF or DOCX.
Send Action Items to Jira, Linear or GitHub With Your Own Script or AI Assistant

Meetily Pro 1.11.0 added four ways for your tools to reach your meetings. Meetily has no native Jira connector and does not file tickets itself: your script or assistant does the writing, with the tracker access you already gave it.

Connect Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor or Windsurf in one click. The assistant can search your meetings, read transcripts and summaries, and start or stop a recording. Ask it to turn yesterday's sprint planning into issues, and if it has its own Jira, Linear or GitHub access, it can file them.
Get an HMAC-SHA256 signed webhook when a recording ends or a summary is ready. A script on your machine verifies the signature, pulls the summary and opens GitHub issues for the action items.
Bundled with Pro. meetily-pro meetings export <id> --format md writes a meeting to Markdown (txt and json also work), ready to pipe into the script that calls your tracker's API.
The API listens only on your computer by default. Your scripts read meetings and summaries locally, and nothing goes to Jira, Linear or GitHub until your script sends it.
Off Until You Turn It On
Nothing is connected until you enable the Automation API in Settings > PRO. Each assistant gets its own permissions and each API key its own scopes. Disconnect or revoke any time.

A custom summary template for standups or sprint planning asks for decisions, owners and action items under the same headings every time, which makes the notes easier for the script that files issues to parse.
The Community Edition is MIT licensed on GitHub, so your team can read how the open source app captures and transcribes meeting audio.
From a sprint planning call to issues in your tracker, with your own tools doing the last step
Start recording, or let Pro detect the meeting and start for you. Meetily captures system audio, so no bot joins the call.
Whisper or Parakeet transcribes on your machine. The summary runs on a local model or your own API key, using a template built for standups or sprint planning.
3. Your Script or Assistant Files the Issues
A script (started by a webhook or using the meetily-pro CLI) or your AI assistant picks up the action items and creates Jira, Linear or GitHub issues with the access you gave it.
From individual developers to enterprise teams
Full Pro access on the engineer's machine, including the MCP server, webhooks and CLI. Transcription runs locally, so meeting audio never goes to a vendor. No card required.
Local transcription - keeps source IP and roadmap conversations on-device
Custom summary templates (sprint planning, retros, design reviews)
Search & replace across standup and review transcripts
Recordings saved locally - no shared workspace by default
Advanced exports for tickets and ADRs
Speaker identification, custom summary templates, PDF/DOCX/Markdown export, and an MCP server, webhooks and CLI for your own scripts and AI assistant.
Connect your AI assistant and your own scripts (MCP, webhooks, CLI)
Best for tech organizations who value privacy and control. Self-hosted with complete data sovereignty.
How Meetily fits standups, sprint planning and incident reviews, and how action items get to Jira, Linear or GitHub.

children.a: Not natively. Meetily has no built-in Jira connector, and it does not create tickets on its own. Since Meetily Pro 1.11.0 your own tools can do it: an AI assistant connected through Meetily's MCP server (Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor or Windsurf) can read a meeting's summary and file the action items using its own Jira access, or a script can export the meeting with the meetily-pro CLI and call the Jira API. The same approach works for Linear and GitHub Issues.

children.q: How do I turn meeting action items into Jira, Linear or GitHub issues?
children.a: Turn on the Automation API in Settings > PRO, then pick a route. Connect your AI assistant over MCP and ask it to create issues from a meeting's action items. Or have a script on your machine listen for the summary-ready webhook, which is signed with HMAC-SHA256 so the script can verify it. Or run meetily-pro meetings export <id> --format md (txt and json also work) and parse the output. Your script or assistant does the writing, so you decide the project, labels and assignees.

children.q: Does a bot join our standups or sprint planning calls?
children.a: No. Meetily records your computer's system audio, so nothing joins the Zoom, Microsoft Teams, Google Meet, Slack Huddle, Discord or Webex call and the participant list looks the same as always. Let your team know when you are recording.

children.q: Does code or roadmap discussion leave the engineer's laptop?
children.a: Transcription runs 100% locally with Whisper or Parakeet, and recordings are saved on your computer. For summaries you choose: a local model keeps everything on the device, while your own API key (BYOK) sends the transcript text to the provider you picked, such as OpenAI or Anthropic Claude. If you connect an AI assistant over MCP, it sends what it reads to its own AI provider. Integrations are off by default, and nothing is connected until you turn it on.

children.q: Can Meetily help with incident reviews and postmortems?
children.a: Yes. Record the incident review, summarize it with a custom summary template that has sections for timeline, root cause and follow-ups, and export the notes as Markdown for your postmortem doc. Speaker diarization shows who said what. Custom templates and speaker diarization are Pro features; the Community Edition gives you the local transcript and a standard AI summary.
Meetily has native apps for Windows and macOS (Apple Silicon). There is no native Linux app. The open source code is on GitHub if you want to build it yourself.

children.q: What does Meetily Pro cost for an engineering team?
children.a: Pro is $10/user/month billed annually (early bird pricing; the regular price is $25/month), with a 14-day free trial that needs no payment. Pro adds speaker diarization, custom summary templates, PDF, DOCX and Markdown export, automatic recording, and the MCP server, webhooks, CLI and local API. The Community Edition is free and open source (MIT) and uses the same transcription engine as Pro. Enterprise, for self-hosted deployment and admin controls, has custom pricing.
